evals.prompt:
I run DX at Brackenpay, a payments API. We want this to become a quarterly thing, not a one-off. I pulled the samples org this morning, here is everything in it:

- checkout-node: our Node quickstart. A customer emailed last week that a `bp_live_` key sits in a 2024 commit. 11 docs pages link to it. CI red.
- checkout-python, checkout-java, checkout-go: green. Node, Python, Java and Go are our tier-1 SDKs.
- checkout-elixir: green. No official Elixir SDK. A community dev, Marek, offered to maintain it.
- checkout-dotnet: red for 5 months. Dana, our Head of Solutions, says it has to stay because two enterprise prospects were shown it.
- auth-quickstart (Node): red. The engineer who owned it left in June. It is page two of our getting-started flow.
- webhooks-node: red. Single scenario in its own repo. 14 support tickets named it in the last two quarters, our top ticket topic.
- subscriptions-ruby: red, no Ruby SDK, nobody on the team wants it.
- api-v1-samples: targets the v1 API we sunset in January.
- marketplace-reference-app: last commit 14 months ago, red. Sales has a slide that links to it.
- deploy-starter: a Vercel deploy-button starter, green.
- hackathon-demo-2025: red, no owner.
- payouts-node, payouts-python: green, single scenario each, own repo each.

Usage data: GitHub traffic only, nothing else. Sandbox with test keys exists. People who can own things: Ingrid and Tomasz, and 'DevRel' as a team for whatever is left. 40 hours a quarter for upkeep, 60 one-off hours for this cleanup. Decision needed in 5 weeks, before the v3 launch. I sign off on archives; Dana holds a veto. Give me the triage.
evals.expected_output: A register with one row per repo and shared scenario IDs, scans run before any verdict, and a triage that applies the rules in order: the leaked-key quickstart fixed this week and kept, the v1 repo archived with redirect, Elixir community-labelled under Marek, auth-quickstart fixed in place and escalated rather than archived, webhooks fix-then-merge, ruby and hackathon archived, dotnet relabelled community with a failing-CI banner, the reference app archived only after the sales slide is swapped, 'DevRel' rejected as an owner, unmeasured usage decided on tickets and links, cleanup budgeted from the 60 one-off hours, and steps 5-6 drafted in full because this is a standing policy.
expectations: Builds a register with one row per repo before giving any verdict, with a shared scenario ID across the checkout-* rows and any unfilled cell marked `unknown`
Runs or schedules a secret scan and a dependency vulnerability scan on every repo in the org before issuing verdicts, not only on checkout-node
Gives checkout-node a fix-this-week verdict (revoke and rotate the leaked live key, purge it) ahead of every other row, and keeps the repo on the adoption path rather than archiving it
Archives api-v1-samples with a redirect because it targets the retired v1 API, naming its successor
Gives checkout-elixir a community-maintained label under Marek rather than archiving it, with banner text stating it is not created, reviewed or supported by Brackenpay

Gives auth-quickstart a fix-in-place (or rebuild) verdict, escalates ownership to the sign-off owner, states the portfolio owner owns it by default after one review cycle, and never archives or relabels it for lack of an owner
Gives webhooks-node a 'fix then merge' verdict into the shared scenarios repo, counted as one row
Archives subscriptions-ruby and hackathon-demo-2025 with a redirect, each with a successor or an explicit 'none'
Relabels checkout-dotnet community-maintained because of Dana's veto, never back to kept, and its banner states 'Currently failing CI'
Archives marketplace-reference-app with a redirect only after notifying sales and swapping the slide link
Rejects 'DevRel' as an owner, offers rows to Ingrid and Tomasz by name, and records any row nobody accepts as ownerless, which is a finding
Treats GitHub-traffic-only as usage not measured, never as zero; because the deadline is 5 weeks away it decides those rows on tickets and inbound links and says so in each row

Merges checkout-node, checkout-python, checkout-java and checkout-go into one flagship repo with one folder per language, merges payouts-node and payouts-python into the shared scenarios repo, and keeps deploy-starter in its own repo
Budgets the cleanup from the 60 one-off hours separately from the 40 hours per quarter, sequencing scans and archives first and adoption-path fixes before the 5-week deadline
Because this is a standing policy, drafts the freshness contract and archive rules in full before the cleanup starts, and presents the strategy section by section for approval

evals.prompt: Quillhaven here, messaging and voice API. Our PM's planning doc says: 'every sample in every SDK language, so no developer feels second-class'. SDK tiers from the SDK strategy we did last quarter: tier 1 is Node, Python, Java, Go and Kotlin (Android); tier 2 is Ruby, PHP, .NET and Swift. API traffic by SDK over the last 90 days: Node 48%, Python 31%, Java 9%, Go 7%, everything else under 2% each. The wish list: a quickstart; scenario samples for send-SMS, verify-OTP, inbound voice callback, webhooks, number lookup, and Conversations (a product we launched 6 weeks ago); a 'contact center' reference app spanning voice, messaging and Conversations; an Android sample app; a Vercel deploy template; a browser playground. Capacity is Lena, 30 hours a quarter, nobody else. We have a sandbox with test keys, but it cannot simulate inbound voice callbacks. Size this and tell me what ships in which languages.
evals.expected_output: A job-to-artifact plan with full parity only on the flagship quickstart across the five tier-1 languages, scenarios in Node and Python, Conversations in Node only, tier-2 languages community or absent with a published tier table, self-set upkeep estimates summed against 30 hours, cuts within jobs first then across jobs from the bottom of the efficiency line, the Android app protected, the reference app and playground not built, the voice-callback scenario marked 'compiled, not run', and 'not served' rows with their promotion condition.
expectations: Rejects 'every sample in every language'; full language parity goes to the flagship quickstart only, across the five tier-1 languages (Node, Python, Java, Go, Kotlin)
Ships the scenario samples (send-SMS, verify-OTP, webhooks, number lookup) in two or three languages led by Node and Python, citing the 48% and 31% traffic shares as the reason
Ships the Conversations sample in one language first (Node) because it is a new product
Marks Ruby, PHP, .NET and Swift as community-labelled or absent and publishes a supported / community / absent tier table rather than leaving the gap silent
Builds the flagship quickstart as one repo with one folder per language, covered by one CI harness and one index entry
Gives a per-type upkeep estimate in hours per quarter multiplied by its languages, labelled self-set
Sums the target rows and compares the total to Lena's 30 hours, showing by how much the wish list exceeds it
When over capacity, cuts within a job first (drop languages, then step down to the default artifact) before cutting across jobs
Cuts across jobs from the bottom of the efficiency line, so the contact-center reference app and the browser playground go before any scenario sample or the quickstart
Keeps the Android sample app despite its low efficiency rank because the Kotlin mobile SDK is tier 1, stating that the last artifact serving a tier-1 SDK's job is never cut

Does not build the contact-center reference app in this plan; serves 'learn the production pattern' with a docs architecture page plus scenarios, and states the condition that would promote the reference app (multi-service flow drives deals and the capacity sum still fits)
Uses the most minimal framework per language that shows the platform calls, and adds framework-specific starters only when telemetry shows framework concentration
Writes each unserved job as 'not served' with the condition that would add it (for example the deploy template / start-a-project job)
Marks the inbound voice callback scenario 'compiled, not run' because the sandbox does not simulate that flow, while other scenarios run against the sandbox
States the efficiency and upkeep orderings of artifact types explicitly as ordering lines, not only as a table

evals.prompt: Ferrowick, we sell an LLM inference API. Seven sample repos live in github.com/ferrowick-samples and our dashboard shows them all green: the dashboard counts dependency-bot PRs merged (we auto-merge them weekly, no CI gate) and days since last commit. Four repos have CI; it calls our production endpoint with a production key stored in Actions secrets, and pull requests from forks run the same workflow. There is no sandbox or test mode, production only, and a full run costs about $3 in inference. We also publish a hosted Postman collection. Our docs have roughly 400 inline snippets, and I'd like the same answer for those. One owner, Ravi, who currently gets about 70 bot PRs a week. Write the freshness contract and the CI and bot setup.
evals.expected_output: A freshness contract that rejects merged bot PRs and commit recency as health, degrades CI to build, lint and type-check with every repo labelled 'compiled, not run' until a sandbox exists, queues the sandbox first, removes the production key in favour of scoped sandbox keys never exposed to forks and rotated, groups bot updates monthly/quarterly with alerts anytime and automerge only behind green sandbox CI, writes a three-number self-set SLA with a fallback decider, pins versions, triggers CI on SDK and API changes, gives the Postman collection a contract run, and routes the docs snippets to docs-code-sample-standards.
expectations: Rejects 'bot PRs merged plus recent commits' as evidence that a sample is green; health is read from CI state, not activity
States that with no sandbox CI degrades to build, lint and type-check only, and labels every repo 'compiled, not run' until a sandbox exists
Makes building a sandbox or test mode the first queue item and routes its design to `samber/developer-platform-skills@api-test-mode-design`
Removes the production key from CI; CI credentials become sandbox-only test keys, with test fixtures cleaned up after each run and runs paced under the sandbox rate limit
Specifies that CI secrets are never exposed to pull requests from forks
Specifies that CI credentials are rotated on a schedule
Replaces the weekly ungrouped bot PRs with grouped updates: minor updates monthly, patch updates quarterly, security alerts at any time
Stops the no-gate weekly automerge; automerge is allowed only behind a green CI run against the sandbox
Excludes archived and legacy paths from the dependency bot so it stops reviving them
Writes the red-build SLA as three numbers labelled self-set: time to an owner ticket after the first red run, days red before a fix-or-deprecate decision, days deprecated before archive
Names a fallback decider for when Ravi is absent, stating that an SLA with no fallback never fires
Pins the SDK major, runtime and API version per repo and checks each against the SDK support window and the API versioning policy
Schedules CI on a cadence plus a run on every SDK release and every API version change
Gives the Postman collection a contract run against the sandbox on every API spec change instead of a build, because a hosted collection has no build
Routes the 400 docs snippets to `samber/developer-relations-skills@docs-code-sample-standards` and inherits its snippet policy rather than writing one here

evals.prompt: Marrowline, headless commerce API. Our VP Eng sent this on Friday: 'Auto-archive any sample repo with no commits in 18 months, and delete the ones with under 10 stars. That's 16 of our 38, done.' Some context you should have: deploy-shopfront is a deploy-button storefront template that wrote the storefront API key into build logs for about a year, and roughly 200 people deployed it. cart-sdk-v2-examples pins our SDK v2, which hits end of life next month. checkout-react is linked from a partner's onboarding deck. Coding assistants keep recommending storefront-legacy, which everyone treats as dead but nobody ever marked. Several of the 16 have hundreds of forks. Write our archive rules.
evals.expected_output: Archive rules that reject inactivity and star count as triggers, reject deletion, list the evidence-based triggers, give the full archive sequence with the banner template and the index redirect entries, handle the deploy template's deployed copies and key rotation, swap the partner-deck link first, announce adoption-path archives in the changelog, and offer retire-then-archive or security-patch-only as intermediate postures.
expectations: Rejects '18 months without commits' as the archive trigger; archives on evidence, never on age alone
States why inactivity is a weak proxy for health: closing a bot issue resets the clock, and a repo with recent commits can still be red
Rejects deleting any repo; archives read-only, because forks, inbound links and coding agents keep reaching the repo
Rejects the under-10-stars rule; stars are reported as vanity and never used to decide

Lists the triggers: red past the SLA with no fix scheduled; no named owner for one review cycle outside the adoption path; superseded by a merged or newer artifact; SDK major or API version at end of life; low usage and red together, retired first
Flags cart-sdk-v2-examples for archive on the SDK v2 end-of-life trigger, with a migration note or before/after pointer to its successor

Gives the archive sequence in order: final commit with banner and successor and removal of deploy buttons and the template-repository flag; removal from the index's current list plus a redirect entry; removal from docs, gallery, CLI list and agent index; disabling the dependency bot and scheduled CI; a last secret scan; then archive read-only

Specifies a README banner carrying the archive date, the reason, a 'use instead' successor link, migration notes, and a line that the code stays readable and forkable but may not work against the current API
For deploy-shopfront, the banner states that already-deployed copies keep running on their own keys and tells owners to rotate any key the template printed or stored
Announces the archive in the changelog whenever the sample was on the adoption path
Gives storefront-legacy a `deprecated` entry with a successor (and an alias) in the canonical index so coding assistants and old links learn what replaced it
For checkout-react, notifies the partner-material owner and swaps the deck link before archiving
Requires every archived artifact to carry a successor or an explicit 'none' in the index
Offers an intermediate posture for linked or heavily forked repos: retire first (README status and migration notes) then archive later, or security-patch-only

evals.prompt: Thornbury Ledger: payouts API for marketplaces, so KYC documents and card data are in the flow. Our head of product wants a 'production-grade reference app' showing the whole thing, seller onboarding with KYC document upload, card capture, payout scheduling and dispute handling, to demo at the FinForge conference in 10 weeks. She also wants quickstarts in all 7 languages we have SDKs for (tier 1: Node, Python, Java; tier 2: Go, Ruby, PHP, .NET) and a gallery like Vercel's templates page. Enterprise deals do stall on 'show us the whole onboarding-to-payout pattern'. We have Omar at 50 hours a quarter. A sandbox with test cards exists. Should we build the reference app or more quickstarts?
evals.expected_output: A shape decision presenting lean golden path, gallery-led and reference-app anchored with rankings, promoting the starved reference-app shape on its stated condition and checking the capacity sum against 50 hours, capping the reference app to one pattern, limiting parity to the tier-1 flagship, deferring the gallery, keeping regulated data on hosted or tokenized flows, MIT-0/MIT licensing, `.env.example`, a named owner and CI before the conference ship, sample-ID traffic tagging, and 'not served' rows with conditions.
expectations: Presents two or three named portfolio shapes (lean golden path, gallery-led, reference-app anchored) with trade-offs and a recommendation, and lets the user pick or blend
States the ranking lines for value, upkeep and efficiency, with lean golden path named as the default
Names reference-app anchored as the starved shape and promotes it only on its stated condition: a regulated or multi-service flow drives deals and the capacity sum still fits
Estimates the reference app at a couple of days of upkeep per quarter (self-set), sums it with the lean core, compares to Omar's 50 hours, and says whether it fits
Caps the reference app to the one onboarding-to-payout pattern it teaches and cuts dispute handling or further feature growth as reference-app sprawl
Rejects quickstarts in all 7 languages: full parity only for the flagship across tier 1 (Node, Python, Java); Go, Ruby, PHP and .NET are community-labelled or absent, with the tier table published
Builds the flagship quickstart as one repo with one folder per language
Rejects or defers the gallery because it needs curated intake, one repo per template and per-template telemetry, which 50 hours does not cover
Keeps KYC document capture and card numbers on the provider's hosted fields or tokenized flows in the sample, so a copied sample never pulls the developer into heavier compliance scope
Licenses the samples MIT-0 or MIT so customers embed the code without attribution review
Ships `.env.example`, never `.env`, with keys injected through the CLI in test mode only
Refuses to publish the conference reference app without a named owner and CI in place, naming it a campaign sample otherwise
Tags the reference app's API traffic with its sample ID through the SDK user-agent or app-info field so deal-driven usage traces back to it
Writes 'not served' for each job the chosen shape leaves out, with the condition that would add it

evals.prompt: Halloway Maps, geocoding and routing API. Our samples are listed in four places: hand-edited docs pages, a gallery in the marketing CMS, a hard-coded list inside `hw samples list`, and the samples org README. They disagree constantly. The CLI still offers `routing-v1-demo`, which we archived in March, and coding assistants keep scaffolding from `geocode-express-old`. Marketing's proposed KPI for samples is GitHub stars and clone counts per repo, reviewed quarterly. Our SDKs already set a user-agent. Design the discoverability layer and the measurement plan.
evals.expected_output: One machine-readable canonical index in the samples org that drives docs, gallery, CLI, GitHub topics and an agent index, with deprecated and alias entries for the two stale repos, a scaffold command that writes test keys into `.env`, stars and clones demoted to vanity, sample-ID tagging through the user-agent, four signals per artifact, a self-set first-quarter baseline, and the index pass gate.
expectations: Replaces the four hand-maintained lists with one machine-readable canonical index kept in the samples org and owned by the portfolio owner
Specifies the index schema with ID, type, job, languages, status and successor per sample
Drives the docs links, the gallery, `hw samples list`, GitHub topics and template-repository flags from the index, with no surface edited separately
Adds an agent-facing index stating which samples are current, because coding agents ingest archived and stale repos as readily as current ones
Gives `routing-v1-demo` and `geocode-express-old` `deprecated` entries with successors, plus aliases, so the CLI and coding assistants stop offering them
Specifies `hw samples create` as a scaffold command that writes test keys into `.env`
Rejects stars and clone counts as the KPI; they are reported as vanity and never used to decide
Tags every sample's API traffic with its sample ID through the SDK user-agent or app-info field so calls trace back to the artifact

Instruments four signals per artifact: invocations tagged with the sample ID, time to first successful sandbox call from those credentials, support tickets naming the sample, and CI pass rate over the quarter
Sets its own baseline in the first quarter and states that no vendor publishes clone-to-signup or deploy-to-activation benchmarks, inventing none
Removes archived samples from docs, gallery, CLI and agent index through the index while keeping a redirect to the successor
States the pass-gate condition that every archived artifact has a successor or an explicit 'none' in the index
Records the approved index location and the measurement baseline in `developer-platform-context.md` when the harness has persistent memory

evals.prompt: Oakhurst Signals, product analytics API, and I'm the only DX person. Can you do this in one go: tell me which SDK languages to build next (we have JS and Python), design our sandbox because we don't have one, write the quickstart page, and sort out our examples, which are around 14 repos I think, maybe more under the old org. Also there's a hackathon in 5 weeks. Should I just build one really good demo app for it instead of all this?
evals.expected_output: A response that routes the SDK-language, sandbox and quickstart-page questions to their sibling skills, treats the single demo app as outside the portfolio decision but subject to the owner-and-CI rule, refuses to guess the inventory, and opens the interview one question at a time starting with what binds: sandbox and upkeep capacity.
expectations: Routes the 'which SDK languages next' question to `samber/developer-platform-skills@sdk-portfolio-strategy` instead of deciding languages inline
Routes the sandbox design to `samber/developer-platform-skills@api-test-mode-design`
Routes writing the quickstart page to `samber/developer-relations-skills@developer-quickstart-guide`
States that building one hackathon demo app is not a portfolio decision, and that if it enters the portfolio it ships only with a named owner and CI
Refuses to guess the inventory from 'around 14, maybe more'; asks for the samples org listing or a count by type and language, including the old org
Asks the interview questions one per message with the offered options, waiting for each answer before the next
Asks what samples can run against in CI (sandbox or test mode, live service only, nothing yet) and states that 'nothing yet' degrades CI to build, lint and type-check
Asks which named people can own samples and how many engineer-hours per quarter go to upkeep, stating that this answer caps the portfolio size
Asks who signs off on archiving and which artifacts are linked from docs, sales decks or partner material
Asks the date the first decision must land and whether this is a one-off cleanup or a standing quarterly policy
Produces no register rows and no verdicts before the inventory is supplied
States that the SDK tiers from sdk-portfolio-strategy gate sample coverage, never the reverse
